"Bourne to inspire others, include everyone and empower ourselves" Nurture. Innovate. Collaborate. Empathise.
Welcome to Bourne Primary School
Bourne is a happy, thriving school that strives to give all children the best education they can receive. We pride ourselves on our diverse community and love to see the children learning from each other.
___________________________________________________________
More information about life at Bourne can be found on the Starting at Bourne Primary page
Please call 01323 724729 or email admissions@bourne.e-sussex.sch.uk to request a visit to our school.
The staff at Bourne school aim to inspire and motivate children through appreciation of all subjects. We believe children learn best when there are high expectations and they are engaged in purposeful and practical activities. Every child at Bourne is respected as an individual and encouraged to take responsibility for their learning and conduct.
We work in partnership with parents and carers and value every child. It is a pleasure to work with such amazing children and see them reach their full potential.
Thank you for visiting our page; we hope you can find everything you need.
Mrs C.Palmer Headteacher

Wrap Around Care
We run wrap around care provision for pupils in Reception to Year 6 that extends the school day from 7:30am to 5:45pm. All sessions need to be pre-booked via the school's Arbor app at least one day in advance so that we can ensure correct staff to pupil ratios.
We also ask parents/carers to complete a Wrap Around Care Registration Form prior to booking.
Please see below for further information or contact the school office on 01323 724729.
Early Birds: Breakfast Club
Open from 7.30am – 8.45am, Monday to Friday, term time only
7.30am or 8.00am at the Melbourne Road gate
Cookery Room/ Hall/ Gym
All sessions must be booked and paid for at least 1 day in advance via the payment option on the Arbor app. Bookings can be made up to 8 weeks in advance
We offer a range of cereals, toast, yoghurt, fresh fruit, fruit juice, milk and water
We offer a range of activities to include games, arts and crafts, construction and puzzles
Night Owls: After-School Club
Open from 3.15pm – 4.15pm, 4.15pm – 5.45pm and 3.15pm – 5.45pm, Monday to Friday, term time only
4.15pm or 5.45pm at the Melbourne Road gate – children can be collected earlier, if pre-arranged
Cookery Room/ Hall/ Gym/ Playground (weather dependent)
All sessions must be booked and paid for at least 1 day in advance via the payment option on the My Ed app. Bookings can be made up to 8 weeks in advance
First session 3.15pm to 4.15pm = £4 / Second session 4.15pm to 5.45pm = £6 / Longer session 3.15pm to 5.45pm = £9
We offer children a drink and a small snack at 3.15pm and 4.30pm – sandwiches / toast / fruit
We offer a range of activities to include games, computers, arts and crafts, construction and puzzles. We will also use the playground when the weather is fine.
We are able to accept Tax Free Childcare - please speak to the office for further information.

The House System
All the children and staff belong to one of the six Houses. Everyone is very proud to be a member of their House.
Every Friday we celebrate who has been working hard to earn points in our House Meetings.
House Captains are Year 6 pupils, voted for by the House at the start of the year. They help to organise the House and run the weekly House meetings.
The House with the most points is announced in our School Values Assembly on Thursday afternoon. The members of the winning House are allowed to wear home clothes to school on the Friday.
The names of our six Houses are taken from inspirational individuals who were selected and voted for by our pupils.

School Uniform
We have two types of school uniform at Bourne Primary School:
Everyday Uniform: this consists of grey or black shorts, trousers, skirt or pinafore with a white polo neck T-shirt and the school sweatshirt or cardigan. Red and white striped or check dresses can be worn in hot weather.
Active Uniform: children wear this on PE days. This uniform consists of red shorts or black tracksuit bottoms, with a plain white t-shirt or Bourne P.E t-shirt and the school sweatshirt or cardigan. We will give you a timetable of PE days at the start of each term.
Footwear: all children should wear black trainers to school. Please ensure your child can take off and put on their own shoes without assistance.
Children should not wear jewellery, make-up or nail polish in school, small stud earrings are permitted. Long hair should always be tied up.
Bourne school uniform is available for sale online from PMG Retail Ltd - https://pmgschoolwear.co.uk/index.php

Training is tailored to support the staff in developing their expertise in meeting the needs of both individuals and groups of children within our setting, ensuring that children are supported effectively through quality first teaching.
To find out more read our Special Educational Needs, Disability and Inclusion Policy for information of how we plan for and ensure outstanding provision for children with special educational needs, disabilities and/ or emotional needs.
Read the school's SEN Information Report for this year's specific information of how we ensure our special needs pupils make good/outstanding progress.
Read our Accessibility Plan for information on how we ensure that we can meet the needs of all learners, staff, parents/carers and visitors to our school and our plans to improve accessibility.

Admissions
Reception to Year 6
Admission of children to any class from Reception to Year 6 (4 to 11 year olds) is arranged through East Sussex County Council. Please follow the link below for more information about how to apply.
Find a school place – East Sussex County Council
East Sussex County Council’s admission arrangements for 2026-27 can be found here: Final arrangements for 2026-27 | East Sussex County Council
Parents/carers may find it helpful to know that, if there are insufficient places available to meet demand, these will be allocated to children in accordance with the following list of priorities:
If it should be necessary to decide between children within any of these priority groups, this will be done by giving the places to those children who live closest to the school.
If your child has special educational needs and has either an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) talk to your SEN Caseworker about which school you would like your child to attend and they will explain the next steps.
Other children.
Nursery
Criteria for Admission to our Nursery
The School Governors will admit children to the Nursery who are a minimum of three years of age. The government fund children in the term after they turn three.
Places are available based on the following criteria:
Within the above criteria, each application is always considered very carefully on its individual needs.
A waiting list will be kept by the school for names, addresses, D.O.B., telephone number and date registered of children. This list will be kept in date of birth order. Parents will be required to complete an admissions form.
The waiting list will not operate places on a "first come, first served" basis. The length of time children are on the waiting list in no way influences the decisions about places.
Each form will be accompanied by an information letter to parents. Completed forms should be returned to the school. Returned forms will be filed in date of birth order.
The September intake into Nursery will be staggered over no more than one working week and home visits will take place during this time. Other places will be allocated on a termly intake system.
Decisions on places will be made by the Headteacher. Decisions will be based on the criteria and procedures laid out in the admission policy and places will be confirmed one term before intake date.
It must be made very clear to parents that the offer of a Nursery place DOES NOT in any way automatically give entitlement to the main school.

The Bourne Team
Bourne Primary School prides itself on its staff team, its commitment to our pupils, to each other and to providing the best possible education for all children regardless of their different starting points.
Please remember we are all here to help, but usually the best person to speak to is your child's class teacher(s).
Our classes are all named after roads in the area, to support our pupils with their knowledge of local places.
